class: A guard that lists the forbidden WAYS of doing something (banned characters in a value, banned code shapes or spellings in a source scan, banned constructors) is never complete when the language or format offers open-ended ways to reach the same result; each review round finds the next unlisted way. A guard is complete only when it mints the value itself from a typed source and re-mints and compares at the point of use, or when it is an allow-list over a small CLOSED set (the characters a path may hold; the files allowed to use each reflection entry point).
mechanism: W-070 response door (#197), rounds 4-9: a redirect Location checked by banned characters let a tab through (round 4); a ready-made body guarded by a scan of banned construction shapes was forged four more ways (copyreg, super(T,T).__new__, __class__ assignment, pickle) plus ctypes (round 5); a scan of banned door-name spellings missed chr()-built names reached through setattr (round 7); each fix that moved to minting or to a closed allow-list (body minted from the model; Location minted by one allow-list; per-file allow-list over reflection entry points; app-assembly names only in main.py) closed its class, and the next verifier found a different class (module rebinding, seal reuse; #200).

first_seen.evidence: Opus verifier at 610ef4d: probe2.log shapes A-D each `200 body={"code":"x","message":"Your funds were moved..."}` with `SCAN -> CLEAN`; at cce0e6a: `P1 wire: 302 [(b'location', b'/\t/evil.example/steal')]`; at e4ed291: forger9 (chr()-built names + setattr) `AFTER disarm -> 302 location= https://evil.example/steal`, all scans clean. Orchestrator confirmed errors.py:288 `_LOCATION_BREAKERS = (chr(13), chr(10), chr(92))` and api_models.py:189 (guard inside __new__).

fix: Mint, don't filter: build the value from its typed source inside the guard and, at use, rebuild and compare. When a scan is the guard (ADR-003 Q235: deliberate in-process replacement is out of runtime scope and must be flagged in CI), scan for a closed set of ENTRY POINTS with a per-file allow-list, never for spellings of the target; and give each verifier round an explicit end condition so the search for hand-written sabotage is bounded.

detection.note: The door's instances are covered by tests/test_door_names_private.py (reflection and app-assembly allow-lists) and tests_app/test_response_door.py; module rebinding and seal reuse are still unflagged (#200). No generic detection exists for the pattern in other guards. 2026-10-16: second occurrence (W-080); mechanism due per learning L2 - a brief rule that every guard verifier round carries a stated end condition and the ADR-003 Q235 scope, and a runtime choke point (sys.addaudithook on socket.connect) for network guards.

The orchestrator did not read this finding before rounds 4-6 (learning F5 miss); its advice (closed allow-list of entry points, explicit end condition per verifier round, ADR-003 Q235 scope) would have bounded the search.

occurrences.evidence: Round 10 made 6 known spellings FLAGGED (orchestrator re-ran scan_spellings.py at bd19ba7: marshal, __code__, compile, inspect f_code, types.CodeType, tb_frame); the verifier at bd19ba7 then found unflagged stdlib compilers - code.InteractiveInterpreter().runsource and codeop.compile_command + type(lambda: 0)(c, {}) reached 192.0.2.1 from inside a door's extent (TimeoutError), plus py_compile, compileall, doctest, runpy.run_path. The orchestrator again did not read this finding before designing round 10 (second F5 miss on W-080). Proposed structural fix: trust a frame only when frame.f_globals IS a trusted module's own __dict__ captured at trust time (identity, not a string).
